problem: The text defines brake mean effective pressure as torque divided by swept volume. That ratio is only proportional to BMEP; the standard definition is brake work per cycle divided by swept volume, which for a four-stroke engine is 4πT/V_d. As written a student who computes T/V_d gets a number about 12.6 times too small and not in the correct relation to the textbook formula.
fix: BMEP is the brake work done per cycle divided by the swept volume of all cylinders: BMEP = 4πT ÷ V_d for a four-stroke engine (2πT ÷ V_d for a two-stroke), with T in N·m and V_d in m³, giving BMEP in Pa. Torque divided by swept volume is therefore only proportional to BMEP, and that proportionality is enough to compare engines of different sizes.

problem: "BSFC is the mass of fuel spent for each unit of power produced" is dimensionally loose: BSFC is mass of fuel per unit of energy (work) delivered, not per unit of power. A student may take the definition literally and think the unit is g/kW.
fix: BSFC is the mass of fuel spent to deliver each unit of energy at the crankshaft — one kilowatt-hour — so its unit is grams per kilowatt-hour (g/kWh).

problem: "a badly matched engine can be thirsty at both" does not say at both what, so the sentence is unclear.
fix: "a badly matched engine can be thirsty at both low and high speed".
